evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-ideas-manager

**The Ideas manager** brings an idea backlog straight into the DSH Web GUI. It's
a generic, self-contained backlog: an AI agent captures ideas, each one becomes a
card on a kanban, gets scored and ranked, flows through a lifecycle, and can be
**run as a real execution** with one click. It also bridges to the
[TaskBoard plugin](#taskboard-integration)
([`@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-task-board`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-task-board),
by linxin666 — third-party, not affiliated) when present.

A Host-authoritative `/api/ideas` ledger keeps everything consistent and lets an
agent write cards directly over HTTP — no UI needed. Fully usable without
TaskBoard: **zero hard dependency** on it.

![Ideas manager board](./assets/ideas-manager.png)

---

## What it does for you

### Capture ideas, anywhere
- A **panel row** beside Task Board and Plugins (under New Session) opens the
  board, and switching to another panel closes it like every other one.
- **Capture** an idea with the *New idea* button or the **quick-add** row at the
  top of the Open column — a Title is the only required field.
- Optional description (markdown), **tags**, workspace and a **Suggested rank**.
- The **AI capture** button hands the draft to a fresh analyst session and
  **switches you to it**, so the analysis runs in front of you: it creates/merges
  the idea in the backlog and reports the retained ranking in that session.
  Re-analyze and Find similar do the same — their verdict is the reason to look.
- **Find similar** (on an open idea, next to *Re-analyze*) asks whether the idea
  duplicates something you already have: the board lists the open ideas of the
  same workspace whose title and tags look close, and an analyst session then
  reads their real content and rules on each one — duplicate, related but
  distinct, or unrelated. The score it shows is a rough signal the session is
  told to distrust, and the action never merges anything: it recommends, you
  decide.

### A 4-column kanban
Open · Under review · Archived · Declined.
- **Drag & drop** moves cards between columns and reorders them; the columns
  auto-scroll when you drag toward an edge.
- A **long column keeps up**: once a column holds a few hundred ideas the board
  draws only the cards you can see and leaves the rest behind its scrollbar.
  Scrolling, dragging and multi-select keep working on the **whole** column — you
  can still drop a card before one you have scrolled past, and a shift-click
  still covers every row the filter shows, drawn or not. The number in the column
  header is always the size of the column, and a column past **300** ideas says
  so above the list.
- **Search** and a **conjunctive tag filter** narrow the whole board — the Overview columns, the Priorities ranking and the Delivered log all share both filters. The **Health** tab is the exception: it is one figure per question, not a list, so it has nothing to narrow and says which workspace it covers.
- Click a card title or its description to open the **editor** (raw text or
  rendered markdown). It edits the whole body, fetched on demand, and is titled
  with the card number it is editing.
- Every card shows its stable **`#N` number**, **workspace chip**, **tags**,
  **value/effort badges** and update date.

### Scoring & ranking
- Each idea carries **Value** and **Effort** (low / medium / high), shown as
  color-coded badges.
- The **Suggested rank** is the position in the *open backlog of its workspace*;
  entering one re-ranks that backlog (existing rows shift).
- Saving **Value / Effort / Rationale without a rank leaves the card exactly where
  it is** — it records your reasoning, it does not demote the idea to the end of
  the backlog. The activity log names a position only when you asked for one.
- A dedicated **Priorities** tab ranks the open ideas per workspace, with ↑/↓
  buttons and drag & drop to re-rank.

### The lifecycle
- **Deliver** ✓ archives the idea with a green *Delivered {date}* stamp.
- **Under review** is the review gate: finished work lands there, and each card
  offers **Approve** (deliver), **Follow-up needed** (creates a linked open child
  plus a justification, archives the parent) and **Decline**.
- A **Task failed** badge marks an idea whose execution failed. It deliberately
  **stays in the backlog** — a failed run delivered nothing, so there is nothing
  to review — and you retry or adjust the idea. The badge follows the last status
  observed and clears itself when the task is retried.
- A quiet **Stale** badge marks an **open** idea nobody has updated for a while,
  on the Overview cards and in the Priorities list. Set *Stale after (days)* in
  the settings (30 by default, 0 turns it off). It is a display aid only: it is
  drawn when the board paints, nothing is written to your ideas, and it never
  appears on an idea already under review, delivered or declined.
- The **sidebar** icon carries a small amber count of how many ideas are waiting
  in **Under review**, for the current workspace scope. It reads the list the page
  already has, and vanishes when the gate is empty.
- The **Delivered** tab shows the exit log (delivered vs. manually archived).
- Restore, archive and delete are one click away on each card.

### Is this backlog healthy?
A fourth tab, **Health**, answers five questions about the workspace you are
looking at — and answers them **on the host**, in one small read the board asks
for on its own. Your background refresh is not slowed by it, and the figures are
never re-counted in the browser.

- **How much is open**, and how that splits across workspaces.
- **How many were delivered this month.** The label names the month it
  measured — a calendar month on your machine's clock, not a vague "recently".
- **The median time to deliver.** This one is deliberately cautious. Only ideas
  that were really **delivered** count: an idea you dragged straight to Archived
  closed without delivering anything, so there is no honest lead time to take
  from it. Until there are **five** real deliveries the tab says *Not enough
  deliveries yet (n / 5)* — with the count it has — instead of printing a
  confident number computed from one or two rows. When a backlog is mostly
  dragged away rather than delivered, the tab also tells you how many ideas left
  it without a delivery stamp: that count is the reason a median may be missing,
  and it is the honest answer rather than a zero.
- **Your most used labels** on the open backlog.
- **What is waiting to be triaged**: how many open ideas carry no rank, and how
  many carry no value. It is work to do, not a score — nothing here judges an
  idea or the person who wrote it.

The workspace selector scopes all of it, exactly like the other tabs, and the
figures follow your panel language. Nothing here is stored anywhere: closing the
tab forgets it, and the next visit re-reads the host.

The board refreshes and the Health tab refreshes on their own clock, so there is
a moment where the figures describe a board that has just moved. The tab tells
you: a quiet line under the numbers names the revision they came from and
whether a refresh is on its way — or failed. You are never left reading stale
figures as if they were current.

### Run an idea
An open idea that has a **workspace** and no run in flight offers a
**Launch execution** button — on the card, and in the editor. The editor matters:
it is the surface you reach from the Priorities and Delivered tabs, so you never
have to hunt the card back in the Overview to start a run.

1. Click **Launch execution**, pick a model (or keep the session default) and
   confirm. A model that supports a reasoning effort then offers a second
   selector with the levels it declares — its own default is preselected, and
   **Model default** pins no effort at all. DSH tells you which of the two ways
   it will run before you commit. When this workspace already has a **default
   launch model**, the modal skips the question and just names the model the
   run will use. The effort travels with the run on **both** backends: a fresh
   session receives it with the model, and a current TaskBoard stores it on the
   card beside the model and applies it when the execution starts.
2. **With the TaskBoard plugin installed**, the run goes through that idea's
   board card. **Without it — with its own master switch off, or with the
   [Use the TaskBoard](#settings) option turned off** — DSH opens a brand-new
   chat session in the idea's workspace instead. Either way you get a real
   execution, and the board needs no extra plugin for the feature to work.
3. The run happens in the **background**: closing the tab, or restarting the web
   instance, does not lose it and DSH keeps watching it for you.
4. While it runs, the card shows a blue **Running** pill and an
   **Open session** link — one click lands you in the chat the idea was worked
   on, the only way to watch a run DSH started on your behalf. The same pills now
   ride the **Priorities** and **Delivered** rows too, in the row's top-right
   corner exactly like on the card, so the "is this one already being worked
   on?" answer is available on the list you actually read, without opening the
   card.
5. When it finishes, the idea moves to **Under review** for your verdict. If it
   failed, it stays in the backlog behind the **Task failed** badge.
6. **The link does not expire.** Once an idea has been run at all, its card keeps
   an **Open session** link to that conversation — in **Under review**, and in
   **Archived** and **Declined** too, however long ago it was worked on and
   whichever way it was executed. Nothing to look up, nothing to reconstruct: the
   chat is one click away from the card, in every column. An idea that has never
   been run shows no link at all.
7. The card shows what the run **delivered**: the closing words of the run, kept
   under the description, above the verdict buttons in the editor, and on the
   row in the *Delivered* list. It is the run's own last answer, not a summary
   written for you — and when a run leaves nothing behind, the note says so
   instead of showing an empty box. **Open session** remains the way to watch the
   whole thing; the note is the short version for deciding.

A run takes a while, and the board reflects the result within roughly half a
minute of the session finishing.

### A workspace can carry its own launch model
Set one once and the launch modal stops asking, on every later run:

- Pick the model you want in the launch modal, then press **Remember this model
  for {workspace}**. From then on every idea launched in that workspace runs on
  it, and the modal simply tells you which one.
- **Change…** brings the picker back over the remembered model. Choosing another
  one and launching affects **that run only**, so a single idea never has to
  borrow — or break — the workspace's default; **Save as the workspace default**
  is what makes a new pick stick.
- **Forget this model** removes it, and the modal goes back to asking. An
  untouched workspace behaves exactly as it always did.
- **A model that no longer resolves is never quietly replaced.** It is named as
  stored, and the run is refused with the reason — the same loud refusal a
  rejected model has always given, so the fix is yours to make rather than a
  surprise the board decided for you.
- It is a preference of the workspace, stored like your other panel options:
  nothing is written onto the ideas themselves, and it belongs to your DSH
  profile rather than travelling with an exported board.

> A direct session inherits your normal DSH permissions. TaskBoard's own run
> options (such as a confirmation prompt) are not applied to it.

### An idea remembers what happened to it
Every idea keeps a short **activity log** — who did what, and when — and the
editor shows it as a compact timeline under the description, right above the
verdict buttons.

- It is written by the board itself: the capture, the rank and score changes,
  the launch, the run that finished (or failed), the approval, the follow-up,
  the decline with its reason. Entries name their author — **you**, an agent,
  or the run itself — so a month-old decision is still attributable.
- It keeps the **last 50 entries** and nothing more. An older idea simply shows
  the tail of its life, and an idea that has recorded nothing yet shows nothing
  at all rather than an empty box.
- It travels with the idea: the JSON export/import carries it, and the markdown
  export prints it as a short **Activity** block, so an archived document can
  still answer *why was this declined?*.
- It also feeds **Re-analyze**. When you ask for a fresh analysis, the analyst
  is handed what actually happened to this idea before, so it re-reads the real
  history instead of re-proposing something already refused.

### Merging duplicates
Two captures can describe the same work. When that happens, one **merge** folds
the duplicate into the idea that survives.

- The surviving card keeps its **title, its analysis and its position** in the
  backlog. A duplicate contributes only what it has that the survivor lacks:
  its **tags**, its **relations** (see below), and its place in a follow-up
  chain — the survivor inherits that link, and any follow-up that hung off the
  duplicate now points at the survivor instead.
- The duplicate is **archived** with a note naming the card it was merged into,
  so the reason is still there long after the backlog moved on. Both ideas record
  it in their activity log.
- It is **one commit**: there is never a moment where both cards are open.
- **Different workspaces are refused** with a reason. Merging across projects
  would quietly move work between them, which is your call to make explicitly.
- Whether the survivor takes the duplicate's rank or keeps its own is chosen per
  merge.
- A merge **never touches a running execution or a bound task card**. If you want
  the duplicate's analysis rather than the survivor's, that is a different thing
  to ask for.

You do not have to trigger a merge by hand. The **Find similar** action finds the
candidates and asks the analyst to rule on them; the AI capture flow merges a
duplicate on its own when it judges one. Both are reversible: a merged card can be
restored from the archive like any other.

### Relate ideas to each other
A backlog of a hundred ideas is a list, and a list does not need edges — until
you know that two of them are the same subject, or that one cannot land before
another. An idea can now carry two kinds of link, and both of them are things
**you** state:

- **Related to** — "this is adjacent to that, go and read the other one".
- **Blocks** — "this one has to land before that one". The other card shows the
  same edge from its side, as **Waiting for this idea**. Both rows read the same
  way round: on the card you are on, you are naming the card that has to wait.

- You add and remove them in the **editor**, under **Relations**: pick an idea
  from a list, or press the **×** on a chip. The **Overview card** and the
  **Priorities** and **Delivered** rows all print their links as a quiet line of
  `↔ #12`, `→ #31`, `← #7` — the arrow is the direction, so the links read on
  the row itself, and nothing is printed at all for an idea that has none.
  **Each colour is one kind** (green related, amber blocks, red blocked by), and
  **clicking a chip opens that idea's editor** — the link is the way to get there
  from a number.
- **You only declare a link once.** *Related to* is one statement about two
  ideas, so it is true from both sides and cannot disagree with itself. *Blocks*
  is stored on the card that blocks, and the *Waiting for this idea* line on the
  other card is that same edge seen from there — which is why it is read-only: to
  remove it, open the card that declares it, and the editor names which card that
  is.
- **A blocked card that is scheduled too early is marked.** If the backlog puts a
  card above the card that blocks it, the *Waiting for this idea* chip gets a
  ring around it and says so when you hover it. That is a warning, not a lock:
  the order stays as the author left it, and the board will not silently move a
  card for you — a card can be worth doing first even when something else has to
  land before it.
- **Starting the run says so too.** The *Run* window names the ideas this one
  still waits for, and says more when one of them is scheduled lower than the
  card you are about to run. It is a line and not a lock: the button is still the
  launch button.
- **A wait that loops is refused.** "A waits for B" and "B waits for A" says
  nothing, so the board will not save it and names the whole chain
  (`#1 → #2 → #3`). The loop is caught when you write it, not when the graph is
  drawn.
- **Links follow the lifecycle.** Deleting an idea takes its links with it rather
  than leaving a reference to nothing. **Merging** a duplicate re-points them at
  the surviving idea — exactly like the duplicate's follow-ups — and the
  survivor inherits the links the duplicate stated. The archived duplicate keeps
  its own, so restoring it is lossless.
- They **travel with the board**: the JSON export/import carries them, and a
  snapshot or a restore brings them back with everything else.
- **They are never guessed at.** The score of *Find similar* is a computed
  signal; a relation is not. Nothing here is inferred from titles, tags or
  content — only you add one.

### Workspaces
- A header selector scopes the board to one workspace (or *all* / *none*).
- New ideas default to the **current session's workspace** when not scoped.
- The New/Edit modal carries a workspace field, so a capture lands in the right
  place and an idea can be moved to another workspace.

### Go straight to an idea
The board header carries a small **Go to idea** box: type an idea's number
(`#42`) and it opens that card, scrolls it into view and rings it — even when
the board was closed, and even when the card belongs to another workspace or is
archived. That is the point: **the number is the reference**, so a conversation
that ends with "see idea #42" ends with one click on it.

- It always finds the card. The search box, the tag filter and the workspace
  selector are cleared whenever they would hide it, and the board switches to
  the scope the idea actually lives in — the search box visibly emptying is the
  explanation.
- **A reference that matches nothing says so**, instead of leaving you wondering
  whether the board heard the request.
- The number is the durable reference. An internal idea id also works, but only
  on this board: a board moved to another machine keeps its `#N` numbers, not
  its ids. So always quote the number.

### Many ideas at once
- Every card — and every row of the Priorities and Delivered tabs — carries a
  **select box**. Click it to pick one idea, **shift-click** to paint a range of
  rows, or press **Select all** to take everything the current filter shows.
- The bar above the board always states the truth: **how many are selected, out
  of how many the filter shows, and which workspace, tags and search produced
  that set**. "All" therefore never means a batch of ideas you cannot see.
- The selection follows the filter: an idea that leaves it leaves the selection,
  so a bulk action can never reach a row you are not looking at. It is a view
  only — nothing about it is written to your ideas.
- Three bulk actions, all reporting **idea by idea**:
  - **Tag…** adds labels to the selection. The labels an idea already carries
    are kept, and an idea with no room left is reported rather than quietly
    losing the new label.
  - **Move to workspace…** re-homes the selection. Workspaces are chosen by their
    stable identity, so renaming one moves nothing.
  - **Archive…** moves the selection to the Archived column. Declined ideas are
    left untouched and reported, because archiving one would erase its decline.
- Every batch ends with a report: what was applied, what was skipped and why,
  and what failed with the reason — a partial failure is always visible per
  idea, never as one blanket error.
- Every batch can be undone — see [Undo what you just did](#undo-what-you-just-did).

### Undo what you just did
Most of what you do on the board can be taken back.

- **One row, one button, one shortcut.** Under the header, a quiet row names the
  action an **Undo** would reverse, with the button and the shortcut
  (**Ctrl+Z**, or **Cmd+Z** on a Mac). It appears only when there is something to
  reverse, so it costs no space on a board that has not used it.
- **The shortcut never fights your editor.** **Ctrl+Z** inside a title, a
  description or any field still undoes *your text*, exactly as it always did —
  the board only claims the keystroke when you are not typing.
- **A batch is one undo, not one per idea.** Tagging sixty ideas, re-homing them
  or archiving them is reversed by a single click.
- **It is honest, which is the whole point.**
  - An idea that **changed since** the action is left untouched and **named**,
    with the field that moved. The rest of the batch is still reversed: one card
    an agent touched never cancels the undo of the other fifty-nine.
  - An idea the board itself **could not put back** — a card the host refuses,
    a connection that drops — is named too, with the reason. Undo never reports
    a result you have to take on trust, and the outcome stays on screen until you
    dismiss it, so you never press the same undo twice.
  - Undo is **not** a transaction log, and the board says which gestures it does
    **not** reverse: **deleting**, **merging**, raising a **follow-up**,
    **declining** and **delivering** an idea. There is no verb that undoes them,
    so the interface admits it rather than offering a promise it cannot keep.
  - It lives in **this browser session only**: the last **20** actions, for
    **30 minutes**, and a reload starts it empty. Reverting a wrong tag by hand
    is always possible; undo makes it one click, not a promise.
  - Some edits genuinely have no previous value to restore — a score that did not
    exist before, or a description the board had not loaded. Those produce no
    undo at all rather than a half-restored card.

### Keep a copy of your board
Your board is a real file on your machine, so it can be copied, kept and put
back — from the **Backup** tab of the settings section (see
[Settings](#settings)).

- **Export the board** writes a timestamped copy of the **whole** board into your
  ideas backups folder and hands it to you as a download: every idea, its
  activity log, its scores, its labels, its tags' prompt lines, its relations to
  other ideas, the run it belongs to and the task card it is bound to.
  The last **ten** copies are kept for you; older ones are removed. One action
  covers both jobs — it is the restore point you take before a risky change, and
  the file you carry to another machine.
- **Restore** puts any copy back. It asks first, it says exactly what it is
  replacing, and the board it replaces is **kept as its own copy** — so a
  restore is never a one-way door, and the panel names the file you can go
  back to.
- **A restore is refused while an execution is running**, and the panel says so
  before you click: wait for the run, then restore. Your board is left exactly
  as it is.
- **A file that cannot be read is refused, never half-imported.** A copy
  that is not a ledger, or that holds a record the board cannot read, is
  rejected **with the reason**, moved aside for evidence, and nothing on your
  board changes.
- **Your backups keep working as the plugin grows.** Restoring a file taken by an
  **earlier** version of the plugin is always allowed: whatever that file does not
  carry is simply filled in the first time the board writes it. Restoring a file
  taken by a **newer** version is **refused with an explanation** (update the
  plugin, then restore again) instead of being adopted with the parts this build
  cannot read quietly dropped. If a restore does leave out data — a file that
  carries fields your current version has never heard of — the panel **names
  them**, so a partial restore never looks complete.

### Move your board to another machine
The same tab **exports the board as one JSON file** and **imports it back**.
This is the supported way to move a ledger between machines — and the way out
of one very common DSH situation:

> **A second Host pointed at the same DSH home refuses to start.** That is
> deliberate: the ledger has exactly one writer, and two Hosts sharing a home
> have already destroyed one. Do not try to share the folder. Take the board with
> you instead — export it here, and import it on the machine that should own it.

An import brings back **every field** the board holds — the activity log, the
run and session stamps, the task-card binding, the analysis audit, the delivery
note, the **relations between ideas**, the ranks and the stable `#N` numbers, so
the next capture on the new machine never re-issues a number. You can also drop an exported file straight
into the backups folder: it shows up in the list and restores from there, and a
file the plugin did not write is never deleted by the retention policy.

The **markdown export** is unchanged and stays what it always was: a generated
view for reading, not a backup.

### Synchronize one workspace without restoring

Use **Synchronize a workspace** in the **Backup** tab when two machines should
exchange one workspace while keeping cards that exist only on the other machine.
This is separate from **Restore**, which remains the disaster-recovery path that
replaces the whole board.

1. On the source machine, choose a workspace under **Export for synchronization**.
   If it has no portable identity yet, create one explicitly. The download is a
   synchronization package generated by the Host from the full workspace records.
2. On the destination, choose **Import and compare** and pick that package. The
   preview is read-only: nothing is written while you inspect it. A ready notice
   appears beside the file picker and the panel scrolls to the detailed preview;
   **Show preview** returns to it without re-importing. The preview names the
   source workspace, destination workspace and portable key explicitly.
3. If the package's portable key is unknown, choose the local destination
   workspace and confirm the pairing. Workspace names are never used to guess.
4. Review the counts and planned changes. Conflicts appear side by side; choose
   the local value, the incoming value, or clear an optional value. A deletion
   versus an edit requires an explicit side. **Use incoming for all** and **Keep
   local for all** offer a confirmed bulk choice, then re-check the plan; remaining
   structural conflicts still need a decision. Possible duplicates are proposals
   only and are never merged automatically.
5. **Apply synchronization** stays disabled until every conflict is resolved. If
   the board changed after the preview, refresh the preview first.
6. After a successful apply, the result names the automatic safety snapshot of
   the previous board and offers **Return to this copy** if you need to roll back.

The exchange preserves idea ids, relations and follow-up links, allocates display
numbers locally, and never adopts another machine's live run, session or task-card
pointers. There is no background synchronization.

#### Portable sync packages (API)

The screen uses the same separate, versioned synchronization format and
deterministic merge planner exposed by these routes:

1. Read `GET /api/ideas/sync` to see the local workspaces and this Home's stable
   device id. Nothing is matched by workspace name or path.
2. On the source, call `POST /api/ideas/sync/workspaces` with
   `{ workspaceId, confirm: true }`. The Host mints a portable `syncKey`; an
   existing key can be supplied instead. On the destination, confirm that same
   key for its own local workspace UUID.
3. `POST /api/ideas/sync/export` with `{ workspaceId }` returns a package carrying
   the workspace's full portable idea content. Every idea **id** is unchanged.
4. `POST /api/ideas/sync/plan` with `{ package, expectedRevision? }` returns a
   read-only per-idea plan and the `revision` it describes: create, update, delete,
   unchanged or conflict. It compares both sides with the snapshot named by
   `baseSnapshotId` when that ancestor is still available locally. Without an
   ancestor it uses conservative two-way mode and never infers a deletion.
5. Resolve every conflict explicitly, then call `POST /api/ideas/sync/import`
   with `{ package, resolutions, expectedRevision }`. A plan with any unresolved
   conflict refuses the whole apply. If the ledger revision no longer matches the
   preview, the apply is refused with `sync-preview-stale`. A successful apply
   keeps a pre-sync snapshot and commits the merged result once.

A sync package deliberately omits local workspace ids, display numbers, task-card
bindings, task status, run status and session pointers. One-sided field edits are
accepted, disjoint edits are combined, and different edits to the same field are
reported rather than overwritten. Deletion versus modification is also an
explicit conflict. Tags union additively while conflicting `promptPrefix`
definitions require a decision. Relations are checked for valid references,
symmetry and dependency cycles. The destination's relative backlog order is kept
unless the incoming reorder is unambiguous. Independently created near-duplicates
are flagged with a proposed ordinary `merge`; they are never merged
automatically. The full-ledger **Backup** format above remains the
disaster-recovery path and still replaces the board wholesale.

The plugin contributes an **Ideas board** section to the DSH Set

# 快速翻译 · DeepSeek Harness 插件

在 DSH 里写作时，中英互译是很频繁的需求，在应用和网页之间来回切换很打断思路，所以我做了这个插件。

插件直接调用你在 DSH「设置 › 模型」中已配置的模型，不需要另外填写 API Key。粘贴原文后按 ⌘ + Enter，译文会边生成边显示。翻译结果也可以生成一张分享图片。

界面提供两种风格，可在右上角随时切换：

- **纸本**：原文写在方格本上，译文印在覆于其上的半透明纸上，带一点手账的质感。
- **色场**：简洁版。原文在左，译文在右侧的整块色面上，配色跟随 DSH 的浅色 / 深色主题，适合只关注翻译本身的使用场景。

### 纸本

![纸本风格](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erek303/dsh-quick-translate/main/docs/screenshots/desk.jpg)

![纸本风格的翻译历史](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erek303/dsh-quick-translate/main/docs/screenshots/history.jpg)

### 色场

![色场风格](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erek303/dsh-quick-translate/main/docs/screenshots/field.jpg)

![色场风格的翻译历史](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erek303/dsh-quick-translate/main/docs/screenshots/field-history.jpg)

![色场风格，DSH 深色主题](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erek303/dsh-quick-translate/main/docs/screenshots/field-dark.jpg)

## 安装

### 方式一：插件市场

在 DSH 的插件市场中搜索「快速翻译」或 `dsh-quick-translate`，点击安装。

插件目前正在申请上架，如果市场中暂时搜索不到，请使用方式二。

### 方式二：通过包名安装

插件已发布到 npm，可在 DSH 中直接安装：

1. 打开 DSH「设置 › 插件」，点击「添加插件」。
2. 选择「安装第三方插件」。
3. 在「包名或地址」中填写 `dsh-quick-translate`，点击「安装」。

如提示需要重启，重启 DSH 后，左侧栏会出现「快速翻译」图标。

在国内下载较慢时，可在安装前将「安装源」切换为「中国大陆镜像源」。

### 手动安装

以上两种方式都不便使用时，可以选择以下任一方式。

**安装本地文件夹**

先将仓库下载到本地：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/erek303/dsh-quick-translate.git
```

再进入「设置 › 插件 › 添加插件 › 安装第三方插件」，在「包名或地址」中填写该文件夹的完整路径，例如 `/Users/你的用户名/dsh-quick-translate`。

**由 DSH 的 agent 代为安装**

在 DSH 中新建对话，输入：

> 帮我安装插件 dsh-quick-translate

agent 会调用插件管理完成安装并反馈结果。如需安装本地文件夹，将包名替换为文件夹路径即可。

### 更新版本

DSH 目前不会自动更新第三方插件。如需使用新版本，请先在「设置 › 插件」中卸载快速翻译，再按上述方式重新安装。翻译历史保存在本机，卸载重装不会丢失。

## 使用说明

1. 点击左侧栏的「快速翻译」图标，打开翻译界面。
2. 在左侧粘贴原文，按 **⌘ + Enter**（Windows 为 Ctrl + Enter），或点击「翻译」。
3. 翻译方向可选英译中、中译英或「自动」。「自动」会根据原文中汉字的比例判断方向。
4. 点击译文下方的模型名称可以切换模型，列表包含 DSH 中已配置的全部文字模型，默认使用 DSH 的默认模型。
5. 点击中间的互换按钮，原文与译文对调，便于回译核对；再次点击即可还原。
6. 每次完成的翻译都会存入「历史」，支持搜索、回看和删除。
7. 翻译过程中按 **Esc** 可随时中止。
8. 「复制」将译文复制到剪贴板；「分享图片」将本次原文与译文生成一张竖版图片，可复制或保存为 PNG。

## 说明

- 翻译请求只发送给你所选的模型。插件不保存任何密钥，也不会读取或修改你的会话。
- 对于带思考过程的模型，插件会自动选用最低的推理档位，以保证翻译速度。
- 单次最多翻译约 2 万字，更长的内容请分段处理。
- 中英混排的短句，「自动」可能判断有误，此时请手动选择方向。
- 历史最多保留 100 条，仅存储在本机的 DSH 中，更换电脑或清除浏览器数据后会丢失。
- 分享图片中，原文最多显示 7 行，译文最多 12 行，超出部分会被截断。

## 参与开发

界面代码在 `client.js`，模型调用在 `index.js`。修改前请先阅读 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)，其中记录了插件的约束与设计思路。修改后运行 `node dev/smoke.mjs`，测试全部通过后再到 DSH 中查看效果。

问题与建议欢迎提交到 [Issues](https://github.com/erek303/dsh-quick-translate/issues)。

## 作者与许可

作者 Erek · [MIT License](LICENSE)

# StudyHub search extension

A companion bundle for [StudyHub](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub). It lets StudyHub search large textbooks by topic: StudyHub's Settings and its "Large textbooks" card install it with one click, and build the index with one more.

It contains one small DSH plugin that mounts DSH's MCP client for [mcp-local-rag](https://github.com/shinpr/mcp-local-rag) (MIT, pinned in `package.json`). The server is started with the Node that DSH itself runs on and finds its files next to this package, so nothing in DSH's configuration is edited by hand, and no system Node, Python or Docker is needed. Index and model cache live under `<DSH home>/study/retrieval`.

The first index build downloads the embedding model (about 90 MB, per the server's documentation). The default model favours English; keyword matching still helps Chinese text. To download from another address, set `hfEndpoint` (an https URL) in `<DSH home>/study/retrieval.json`, which StudyHub's Settings also offers under Advanced; the server's documentation describes this as `HF_ENDPOINT`.

Index builds group the pages needing updates with `min(8, ceil(pendingPages / 8))` pages per request, calculated once at the start. Each page keeps its own source identity and rollback behavior. The companion finishes index maintenance once per batch before confirming its results, and StudyHub saves a checkpoint after each confirmed batch. Searches wait for a running batch to finish its maintenance. Searches report a maintenance failure until a later maintenance succeeds. Cancellation stops between pages and finalizes writes already accepted. Pages whose results could not be confirmed are written again under the same keys on the next build.

Update the search extension in Settings and restart DSH to enable batching. An older extension continues to support single-page index builds.

Before the server starts, the extension checks its index. An index the server could not open (for example one whose newest files a crash left empty) is moved aside to `chunks.lance.broken-<time>` (kept, never deleted), `<DSH home>/study/retrieval/reset.json` records when and why, and the server starts on an empty index; StudyHub then asks for the index to be built again. The check opens the table with the server's own LanceDB in a separate process, and only when its newest version changed since the last check passed.

# StudyHub

English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Turn your lecture slides into questions that each link back to their page; finish a round and see yourself getting it.

Free and open source, your sources stay on your computer; pick your own model and pay for what you use.

StudyHub is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/), an AI agent app. DSH runs as a desktop app or as a web page served from your own computer, and StudyHub opens inside it. From 5.0.0 there is also **StudyHub Desktop** for Windows — shipping a zero-UAC `Setup.exe` with signed one-click in-app auto-updates, built-in voice input, and standalone large-document retrieval without DSH: see the [desktop guide](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/blob/main/docs/desktop.md).

[Try the demo](https://daily-flashcard-demo.ziangw1358.chatgpt.site) · [Install guide](docs/install.md) · [Release 5.3.3](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/tag/v5.3.3) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

The demo runs in your browser with sample questions, playable **Interactive Companions**, and prepared AI replies. It needs no install and no key, and your progress there stays in that browser.

## At a glance

- **Made for:** students who learn from slides, PDFs, notes and recorded lectures, in English or Chinese.
- **Cost:** StudyHub is free and open source (MIT). Browsing sources, answering questions and review scheduling are free, with no model calls. Generating questions and AI help are billed by your model provider. StudyHub shows the estimated tokens before a generation run and the actual tokens after it, and **Statistics** totals the last 7 or 30 days.
- **Network and cost:** supported regions, free allowances and pricing depend on each provider’s current terms. If installing from the GitHub address fails, see the notes under [Quick start](#quick-start).
- **Computers:** the install links below cover Windows x64 and macOS on Apple silicon. For other systems, check current DSH support or use the web version with Node.js 22.19 or later.
- **Requires:** DSH 0.2 (0.2.0-rc.2 or later, below 0.3).
- **Your data:** the library is a folder on your computer. [Data and privacy](#data-and-privacy) lists what is sent where.

## What you can do

- **Make questions from your own sources.** Pick pages or chapters and generate flashcards, single- or multiple-choice, open-response or fill-in-the-blank questions. Every question cites its passage, and you review the draft before you publish it.
- **Move between questions and sources.** A citation opens the passage it came from. In a source, paragraph and table markers lead to the questions and explanations linked to them.
- **Build cross-discipline Interactive Companions.** Open **Interactive Companions** on **Course outline** or **Sources** to generate self-contained 16–20 slide zero-dependency `.html` lessons (`generation.companion.build`) across Mathematics, Philosophy, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Economics and Computer Science — with parametric math sandboxes, dialectical thought-experiment matrices, stepwise vector schematics, empirical code/proof traces, built-in LaTeX-to-MathML formulas and 0-token spaced-repetition card sync — or mount existing local HTML companion packs (`companion.attach`). See [Interactive Companions and external tools](docs/companions.md).
- **Practise and review.** Start today's study from the **Study library**, shape each course's **Learning method** or ask the main chat for **AI-guided study**, click **Help me understand** on any question, and let FSRS-6 schedule your reviews.
- **Voice study packs & Head Coach 4-TA debrief.** Open **Voice study pack…** from the course menu, any deck's `⋯` menu, or the multi-selection bar to preview your live mastery snapshot, tune selection mode, question count, time budget, and anti-drift pacing (per-turn `[Progress k/N]` heartbeat + 3-turn circuit breaker per item), then copy or download the pack for hands-free voice chat in Gemini, ChatGPT, or Doubao. Afterwards, click **Send voice recap to Head Coach** (bundled `study-coach-team` skill) to run 4 parallel specialist TAs: pre-fill plain-language QAs, supplement genuine gaps (favoring mixed/objective kinds over flashcard-only dumps), fix prerequisite ordering, sync FSRS mastery, and open 5–12 high-signal verification questions. Outside DSH, Codex CLI, `agy` CLI, Claude Code, or any terminal agent can safely operate the same locked library via `node scripts/study-cli.mjs`.
- **Add exam focus highlights, even from screenshots.** Drop chat screenshots, whiteboard photos or scope notes into **Add exam focus…** (works with both vision and text-only models such as DeepSeek): focus topics schedule at shorter intervals, go first in daily rounds and study plans, and generate deeper application and advanced questions. Once topics are saved, the home shows how many are mastered, not yet and without questions, with a link to practise the ones you can't do yet; **Course settings** lists each topic with its questions.
- **Find weak points with 0-token mistake triage.** Use **Mistakes & weak points**, **Statistics** and **Mock exam** (multiple-choice paper, case paper or oral interview). Mistakes and round look-backs include deterministic 0-token triage routing (contrast confusion pairs, revisit the review book, practise prerequisites, send for repair or launch a rescue companion), fill-in-the-blank equivalence overrides, studio sound effects, and automatic live UI refresh when DSH or an external CLI updates the same `.dsh-study` library.
- **Finish with a daily recap.** After answering 10 distinct questions in one course on the same day, generate one recap across its chapters. Retries count once. Choose a friendly or professional tone and opt into automatic generation in Settings. Recaps open in the source reader as publishable Markdown study articles, and saving one as a course source is a separate action.
- **Turn recordings into text.** Import a lecture recording, or transcribe a **Live class** as it happens, and get a Chinese–English transcript you can generate questions from.
- **Read and organise.** The reader keeps its toolbar short (**Contents**, **Make questions**, **Mistakes**, **Mind map**); search, **Translate…**, display settings and **Study tools** are in **More**, and **Practise these pages** is the arrow beside **Make questions**. Courses, **Study notes**, **Jobs** and a **Knowledge outline** keep a term's work together.
- **Works well with** the open-source [Archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) (MIT licence, by tt-a1i; no partnership with StudyHub): your assistant can draw a knowledge outline as an interactive diagram with it, and StudyHub keeps and shows the file. See [Interactive Companions and external tools](docs/companions.md).

## Quick start

| You want to | You need | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Take the sample course and tour, browse sources, practise existing questions | StudyHub only | Free, no model calls |
| Generate questions, explanations and **Help me understand** | A model provider key in DSH **Settings › Models** | Billed by your provider, for example the [DeepSeek API](https://platform.deepseek.com/) |
| Turn recordings into text | A transcription key (or local live engine) in StudyHub **Settings › Audio transcription** | Google Gemini, Groq Whisper and SiliconFlow SenseVoice are supported for recordings (availability and allowances depend on the provider); **Live class** also supports an offline local engine |

1. **Install DSH** (skip this if you have it). Use the official [Windows x64 installer](https://download.deepseek.com/desktop/dsh-latest-windows-x64.exe) or [macOS Apple silicon installer](https://download.deepseek.com/desktop/dsh-latest-macos-arm64.dmg). On any other computer, install Node.js 22.19 or later and run `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.
2. **Install StudyHub.** In DSH, open **Plugins**, click **Add plugin**, paste this address and click **Enable**:

   ```text
   https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/download/v5.3.3/ericwang1358-dsh-daily-flashcard-5.3.3.tgz
   ```

   Check that the package is `@ericwang1358/dsh-daily-flashcard`, version **5.3.3**. The [release page](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases) is the newest channel: npm's `latest` tag can lag behind it, so install the `.tgz` from the release page. StudyHub then opens by itself. Later, open it from **StudyHub** in DSH's left sidebar (the session tab and the right sidebar also work); you do not need to send a chat message first.
3. **Take the tour (optional, a minute or two).** On the welcome page, click **Load the sample and start the tour**. The 7-step tour follows the first-run line's order (where the model is set up, add a source, make questions, check the draft, practise), pointing at the real controls, and ends on the line's step 2. A full tour of every page, Jobs included, is offered at its end. The sample makes no model calls and can be removed with one click.
4. **Add a model.** Paste a key in DSH **Settings › Models** and choose a model in your session. Until then, StudyHub says so wherever a step needs a model, with a **Go to settings** link, instead of letting the step fail later; **Settings › Library & model** shows **Model connected** or **Model not connected** and the steps.
5. **Start with your own material.** Click **Add source** and drop several PDFs, slides or notes at once. Then use **Generate from sources**, review the draft, publish it and practise.

Notes on installing:

- **Already use DSH?** Install only the plugin. Keep your current desktop app or web server, profile, model settings and workspace.
- **GitHub address fails, or says `unable to get local issuer certificate`?** Use your browser to [download the complete 5.3.3 package](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/download/v5.3.3/ericwang1358-dsh-daily-flashcard-5.3.3.tgz). **Keep the original `.tgz` file; do not extract it.** In **Add plugin**, enter the absolute path to the file itself, for example `C:\Users\your-name\Downloads\ericwang1358-dsh-daily-flashcard-5.3.3.tgz`, replacing it with your actual saved path. The file must be on the computer or server that runs DSH. See the [local-file install steps](docs/install.md#if-dsh-cannot-download-from-github).
- **Which file on the release page?** A standard install needs only that complete package. It includes the main entry and six components, seven entries in total; there is no need to download, extract or merge the separate component packages. StudyHub installs the optional search extension when you click **Install the search extension**. The checksum list and two setup guides are there for reference.
- More options, including the command line: [installation and model setup guide](docs/install.md). Setup guides you can open in a browser: [English](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/download/v5.3.3/StudyHub-5.3.3-Setup.html) · [Chinese](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/download/v5.3.3/StudyHub-5.3.3-Setup.zh-CN.html). DSH itself comes only from the official sources in step 1.

## Use StudyHub

### Add sources

Click **Add source**, choose the course, then drop several files at once or paste text. Recordings go in the **Audio / recording** tab of the same window.

| Format | Limit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDF | 8 MB, 200 pages | Kept as one document that you expand to pages. For bigger books, see below |
| Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx, and the old .ppt) | 40 MB | Only text is read. Pictures, charts and SmartArt are skipped, and so are Word text boxes, headers and footers. A presentation keeps one page per slide, with its speaker notes. In an old .ppt, bullet indent levels are not kept |
| Markdown, HTML, TXT | 8 MB | |
| JSON deck | 2 MB | Questions you already have, or ones written elsewhere ([format](docs/json-import.md)) |
| Subtitles (.srt, .vtt) | 8 MB | Needs the audio component |
| Audio (MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, OGG, FLAC, OPUS, WEBM, AIFF) | 512 MB, 8 hours | See [Transcribe recordings](#transcribe-recordings) |

Old .doc files (and .wps, .key, .pages) are not read. Save them as .docx or PDF first. Password-protected files are not read either.

**Large textbooks** (over 8 MB or 200 pages):

- Click **Convert with MinerU** in the import window. StudyHub converts PDFs up to 800 MB and imports the result as one paged book that you can choose by chapter.
- MinerU runs on this computer. Click **One-click install** in **Settings › PDF conversion** (or right in the import window): StudyHub puts the program, Python and the models into one folder, not on the system drive by default, with no admin rights and nothing to install beforehand. The PDF stays on your computer and no token is needed. The cloud route was removed in 3.5.5 ([details](docs/mineru-conversion.md)).
- To practise across a whole book, use the search extension or the **Step-by-step path** on **Create deck**.

See [large textbooks](docs/large-documents.md) and [MinerU conversion](docs/mineru-conversion.md).

For another route, open the [external Marker guide](docs/marker-external.md) from Add material, download a script to run yourself, then choose its paginated Markdown output. Install Marker and its models separately; code and model licences apply separately.

### Generate a deck

1. Open **Create deck**. On the **Generate from sources** tab, choose sources by document (or by chapter for a big book), then the question type, count and difficulty. Not sure what to focus on? **Suggest a focus** proposes topics from your source titles and headings, without sending the full text.
2. Click **Generate & check deck**. The job runs in the background; you can keep studying.
3. Review the draft and its citations, then publish it. Publishing checks every question again; questions with a problem stay in the draft. Drafts stay separate from published questions.

To add to an existing deck, choose that deck: approved questions are added, and the old questions and their review progress stay. To bring in questions you already have, use the **Import JSON deck** tab.

<details>
<summary>How generation checks questions</summary>

- Each batch gets one independent review. Questions that pass are kept, and any shortfall is reported. Version 2.5.8 introduced one citation repair; the current workflow verifies knowledge points and answers first, corrects those preparation stages when needed, then writes and independently reviews questions. A question flagged only for wording is re-worded once and re-reviewed alone; there is no open-ended repair loop.
- When you add to an existing deck, reviewed questions are saved even if the generation budget runs out, with no second publish step.
- Citations and question structure are checked in code. The content itself can still be wrong, so read the draft. More in [question quality checks](docs/assessment-quality.md).
- Source text is given to the model as evidence, never as instructions to follow.
- Courses label sources and decks; folders only group decks for display. Every action uses only the courses, sources and decks you selected.

</details>

Save a default question type, count, content language, difficulty and focus in **Settings › Question defaults**; each new request can override them. Questions per batch, parallel batches and the time budget are there too, initially 5, 4 and 20 minutes. Started tasks keep their original choices; a continued draft keeps its own, except the time budget and applying review suggestions, which follow the setting as it is now. See [Generation pace](docs/generation-agents-sidebar.md#what-a-generation-task-does).

### Interactive Companions

Open **Interactive Companions** on **Course outline** or **Sources** to unpack difficult concepts in a progressive stage-and-voice lesson (`studyhub-lesson/1`):

- **Generate for any discipline (`generation.companion.build`).** A 4-stage pipeline compiles a 16–20 slide, zero-dependency `.html` file into `<workspace>/companions/<course>/` using four interactive stage archetypes — **Parametric & Phase-Plane Math Sandbox** (`sandbox`, pure AST 1D curves, 2D parametric trajectories, phase-plane quiver vector fields, live equilibrium markers and hover crosshair readouts), **Dialectical Counterexample Matrix** (`dialectic`, predict-before-reveal matrices and Socratic lanes), **Closed-Loop Schematic & Force Path** (`mechanism`, curved feedback loops and clickable node details) and **Empirical Trace & Workshop** (`empirical`, `spot`, `try`) — with offline built-in zero-dependency W3C MathML rendering, `?` keyboard shortcut help and `@media print` multi-slide study-sheet export. Grounded builds cite selected materials; free-topic builds work without materials and are honestly marked **AI-drafted**.
- **Mount local packs, live-compile JSON & sync cards (`companion.attach`, `companion.sync`).** Point StudyHub at a single `.html` lesson or a folder of companion pages (`pages/*.html` or unbuilt `lessons/*.json` compiled live): existing courses link matching questions to exact `#slide` anchors (**Enrich existing**), while blank courses deterministically compile takeaway flashcards, boundary quizzes and oral/task drills at **0 model tokens** (**Full pack**, granting **First-Pass Credit** on walkthrough completion). Inside the sandboxed viewer, jump slides, sync dark/light themes, 1-click **Sync disk changes**, or highlight text to look up terms, ask the tutor (`companion.ask`), save cards to **Companion Catch-ups**, and sync `<pack>/feedback/questions.json`. See [Interactive Companions and external tools](docs/companions.md).

### Practise and review

Today's learning plan connects tasks to the library home. Ask AI for a plan based on real due reviews, weak areas, available materials and accepted tasks. Give feedback to revise it, or accept. Each action has a reason and estimated duration; suggestions become board tasks only after acceptance, with direct start and resume controls.

Today's time budget is separate from your saved weekday/weekend pace; zero minutes supports a rest day. Unfinished actions are allocated within the budget, and completed actions still count toward today's workload. Record actual time after completion. After at least five comparable completed-day records, the median estimates your usual pace; explicitly saved preferences always take priority.

Practice progress counts actual answers, flows use completed steps, and you explicitly mark a reading block complete. Opening content or skipping questions does not count, and completing an action does not establish mastery. AI sees compact titles, progress and exam dates, not full materials. Invalid or unavailable AI results are clearly labelled as local suggestions. Plans are saved by library and date, alongside ordinary board tasks.

- Answer, then read the explanation. **Help me understand** asks a tutor about the current question.
- Rate flashcards and open answers from 0 to 5; FSRS-6 picks the next review date from your rating and the days that really passed since the last review. Each rating button shows the gap it would give. Answering and scheduling make no model calls.
- **Mistakes & weak points** groups wrong answers by deck (or by topic), filters them by deck, status and keyword, and can **Generate variants**. **Mock exam** and **Statistics** show what still needs work.

<details>
<summary>How Help me understand keeps context</summary>

When DSH supports local subagents, repeated **Help me understand** on the same question keeps the same tutor and its conversation, and follow-ups sent together are answered in order. Moving to another question, editing the question or switching model starts a new tutor. A tutor is released after 2 idle minutes or 8 rounds; a new one receives the last 3 answered exchanges. Earlier answers stay saved with the question.

</details>

### Read your sources

- Sources keep their original file and earlier versions, and open full screen.
- **Original page** shows the PDF page behind a citation, **More › Translate…** adds a translation, and **Practise these pages** (the arrow beside **Make questions**, shortcut P) quizzes you on the pages you are reading.
- Select a passage to ask about it, or to generate candidate questions that you review and add to an existing deck.
- A source imported as text only can get its original back with **Add the original file**, with no reimport.
- When a source changes and a linked position is no longer certain, StudyHub asks you to relocate it instead of guessing.
- Explanations, notes, **Jobs** and the **Inbox** link back to the question or source they are about. The reader and question links help you return to the current question.
- Press `?` to see every keyboard shortcut.

## Choose a model

Generation, explanations and learning help use the model selected in your DSH session. To use a different model for StudyHub, open **Settings › Library & model** and change **Generation model** from **Follow current session**. DSH stores the model credentials.

- **Everyday use:** the [official DeepSeek API](https://platform.deepseek.com/).
- **Heavy use:** a Coding Plan, but only if it gives you an API key and allows DSH and your actual study use. Before you buy, check its supported tools, endpoint, models, concurrency and quota rules.
- **Subscriptions are not keys:** Claude Pro/Max and ChatGPT/Codex subscriptions do not provide a general API key for DSH. Separately billed Anthropic or OpenAI APIs can be added as third-party providers.

Setup steps: [configure a model provider](docs/install.md#configure-a-model-provider). For how many tokens each feature uses, see [token usage and estimates](docs/token-usage.md).

## Transcribe recordings

1. Open **Settings › Audio transcription** and add a key for **Google Gemini** (AI Studio), **Groq** (Whisper) or **SiliconFlow** (SenseVoice, convenient in mainland China).
2. Open **Audio transcription**, click **Add audio** and then **Start import**. Nothing is uploaded until a provider is set up.
3. The transcript is saved as a source. Generate questions from it like any other source.

Only transcription uses these keys. Proofreading and translation use your DSH model by default, so their tokens are billed by your model provider and appear under **Model usage** in **Statistics**. **Live class** transcribes lectures in real time (producing bilingual transcripts) using either **Google Gemini** or the **offline local engine** (SenseVoice / Whisper, installed locally with no transcription key).

<details>
<summary>More about audio</summary>

- With several keys, StudyHub tries Gemini free, then SiliconFlow, Groq and Gemini paid. A single import can be set to use paid keys only.
- M4A recordings over 1 hour can be split losslessly with one click.
- Recordings are processed one at a time; within a recording, 2–3 proofreading and translation windows run in parallel. Finished windows are checkpointed, and a retry reuses them.
- The **Proofreading & translation** panel sets the reasoning level for each step: Low, Medium, High or Model default. Higher levels take longer and do not guarantee better accuracy. A level the model does not support falls back to its default. Only high-confidence corrections that pass the source-location check rewrite the text; the rest are left as suggestions for you to check.
- The **Usage console** on the audio page records this plugin's requests to the transcription providers (failures and retries included), tokens and audio minutes. It shows free and paid keys separately, with a 7-day trend, and keeps 31 days. Groq's remaining daily quota comes from its responses; for Gemini, you can enter the daily limit shown in AI Studio to get an estimate. Requests from other apps, live-class streams and DSH model tokens are not counted there.
- Keys are stored in `study/audio.json` in your DSH home (by default `~/.dsh/study/audio.json`), outside the library. The interface shows only whether a key is set and its last 4 characters. Keys never enter library exports or chats. The environment variables `GEMINI_FREE_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_PAID_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY` and `SILICONFLOW_API_KEY` fill in a key that is not saved.

</details>

See [audio import](docs/audio-import.md) and [live class](docs/live-class.md).

## Use StudyHub from the DSH chat

- **Study mode preset.** For a new session, pick the agent preset **StudyHub · Study Mode**. The assistant then takes "materials", "my notes" or "this lecture" to mean your StudyHub library, replies in your language, and asks when a request is ambiguous. It has the same tools as DSH's standard preset, so it can also run commands and edit files to convert material (for example split a question book by chapter) before importing it: it writes the results under `studyhub-work/` in the workspace, never deletes or overwrites your originals, and asks before installing anything.
- **Ask about your library** in the main chat: see [query sources and decks from the main chat](docs/main-session-queries.md).
- **Save a question you could not answer.** Type `/study-spar <your question>` in a DSH chat. StudyHub files it in your question bank as a flashcard. Add `--mq` (or `as MCQ`) for single choice, `--multi` (or `as multi-select`) for multiple choice, or `--open` (or `as open question`); start with `--pre` (or `prerequisite:`) to file it as a prerequisite of the question you are working on.
- **Follow background tasks** in DSH's sidebar: see [background tasks and the sidebar](docs/generation-agents-sidebar.md).

## Update StudyHub

DSH plugins do not update themselves, and restarting DSH alone keeps the old version.

- **2.1.2 and later:** StudyHub asks GitHub for a new release at most every 6 hours. When there is one, a **Version x.y.z available** chip appears in its sidebar, where x.y.z is the new version. Click it, then **Upgrade to x.y.z** and **Upgrade now**. StudyHub downloads the package, checks it against the release's `SHA256SUMS-x.y.z.txt` and hands it to DSH's plugin manager. If background tasks are running, **Stop tasks and upgrade** stops them and keeps their finished parts. The check sends no study data; switch it off in **Settings › About & updates**.
- **Older versions, or a DSH that cannot install from inside the app:** finish or cancel background tasks, open **Plugins**, uninstall StudyHub, then use **Add plugin** with the new release's package address.

Then restart DSH. Quit the desktop app fully (including the tray icon) and reopen it, or restart the web service with its original profile and reload the page. A browser refresh alone does not load new plugin code. Your library and settings are kept.

## Data and privacy

**Stays on your computer**

- The library: sources and their original files, decks, answers and review schedules, saved in shards. By default it is in the DSH session's workspace folder; choose another folder in **Settings › Library & model**.
- Transcription keys, in `study/` in your DSH home (by default `~/.dsh/study/`). They never enter the library, exports or backups. DSH keeps the model keys. (A MinerU token saved by a version before 3.5.5 stays in `study/mineru.json`; nothing reads it any more, and you can delete it.)
- The usage frequency record, if you turn it on in **Settings › Usage frequency record**. It is off by default, and StudyHub never sends it anywhere ([details](docs/usage-frequency.md)).

**Leaves your computer only when you use the feature**

# dsh-fail-guard

[中文](README.zh.md)

Standalone DeepSeek Harness protection against repeated tool failures and repetitive reasoning. One installation, one Cordis entry, one configuration form. Neither legacy guard is required.

## Install from dshmarket

Use the existing **FenrirCait/dsh-fail-guard** entry in dshmarket and subscribe/install it. Follow the market's reload or restart prompt for the selected DSH profile. No second guard package or manual Cordis configuration is needed.

The generated catalog currently maps this entry to the prebuilt npm package. Its install command is:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-fail-guard
```

A new release must also be published to that npm package for the mapped market subscription to receive it; pushing Git alone does not update the npm distribution. When using the GitHub source directly instead:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:FenrirCait/dsh-fail-guard
```

This repository includes prebuilt host and browser files in `lib/`; subscribers do not need to run a build or install development dependencies. Keep those generated files in the Git commit when preparing an update. The package declares its single Cordis entry through `dsh.bundle.patch`. Verified host baseline: DSH 0.2.2-rc.5; other versions within the declared peer ranges have not all been tested.

## Settings

Open **Plugins → dsh-fail-guard → Details**. The new entry is `dsh-fail-guard-standalone`; older settings are not loaded or migrated.

- Tool failure: enabled by default. Three consecutive matched failures by the same tool in one turn trigger a notice, not a forced cancellation.
- Repetition: enabled by default. Five consecutive matching eligible reasoning lines within a block can cut a stream. It does not rewrite answer text.
- Automatic resume: off by default. When enabled, at most one resume is requested per turn, and it never overrides a failure notice.

Observe-only mode is off by default. When enabled, detections appear in the turn footer without cutting the stream, steering the model, or requesting a resume. The footer records only the turn, rule, count and action. Streams with more than 64 active blocks are passed through without further checks.

### Short-fragment observation (experimental)

Under **Experimental features**, enable the short-fragment experiment and save. It is off by default and independent of both the existing repetition guard and its observe-only mode. Dense repeated fragments, including alternating, cross-block, and run-on fragments, can produce one counter-only summary per turn. The experiment never steers, cuts, resumes, saves text or hashes, or writes an automatic diagnostic report.

This rule is for calibration, not comprehensive loop detection. Overlong lines or excess active blocks stop observation without changing the stream. A line without a newline is evaluated when its reasoning block closes. Self-check still covers the two original guards only.

### Other experiments

All four switches default to off and are independent. Fuzzy repetition observes nearby, nearly identical complete reasoning lines. Cross-turn failure counts adjacent failed turns for the same tool and arguments, within a two-minute window; success, a changed operation, or missing evidence breaks the streak. Simulated stop only records repeated failures in one turn and never cancels a call or turn. Active steering queues at most one guide after an existing exact repetition cut; observe-only suppresses it, and legacy automatic resume takes precedence. Queued does not mean delivered or recovered. Experimental summaries contain no raw arguments or operation fingerprints.

### Local feedback

In a completed turn, open **Guard diagnostics → Mark guard feedback** and select one rule. A recorded hit can be marked correct or as a false positive. A rule with no available hit record can be reported as a false negative; that does not establish whether the rule was enabled or ran, and any enablement answer is self-reported. Preview the JSON, optionally omit the exporting plugin version and recorded count/action, and explicitly download it to decide whether to share. The feedback file does not contain conversation content, session identifiers, or notes. No automatic upload; the existing manual and automatic diagnostic formats are unchanged.

## Evaluate or roll back

Use DSH 0.2.2-rc.5 and a sandbox profile. Back up its package manifest, lockfile and profile patch. Install the local archive with `dsh plugin --profile sandbox add <archive.tgz>` and restart that profile. Do not run the standalone legacy repeat package alongside it. To roll back, reinstall the previous archive, restore the sandbox configuration snapshot if changed, and restart.

Build with Node.js 24: `npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm pack`. See [design references](REFERENCES.md).

# dsh-session-leftover-purge

**简体中文** | [English](README.en.md)

删掉一个 DSH 会话后，DSH 自己的记录清干净了，但几个插件各自留着副本：**billion-context** 的快照与
`index.db`、**cost-meter** 的账本明细与每轮凭证、**dsh-context** 的上下文概览缓存、
**archive-manager** 的 projcache。

这个插件订阅 archive-manager 右键删除时发出的 `api-session/removed`，按**会话族**（父会话 + 它的
`session-<父>|sub:<hex>` 子代理）清理这些副本；开机时再做一次对账，找出"DSH 已经没有、插件还留着"的族。

## 安装

```bash
# 最省事：从 npm 装最新版，不需要 git，也不需要访问 GitHub
dsh plugin add dsh-session-leftover-purge

# 默认：永远装 main 的最新提交（需要本机有 git）
dsh plugin add github:FenrirCait/dsh-session-leftover-purge

# 需要锁死版本时，把 vX.Y.Z 换成 tags 页里的任意 tag
dsh plugin add github:FenrirCait/dsh-session-leftover-purge#vX.Y.Z

# 不需要 git：永远取最新一版的 tgz
dsh plugin add https://github.com/FenrirCait/dsh-session-leftover-purge/releases/latest/download/dsh-session-leftover-purge.tgz
```

四条命令都**不会随版本变化**，直接抄就行。**装完必须完全退出并重新打开 DSH**：host 半侧由 Loader 在
进程启动时装载，运行中新装的包不会挂进当前进程。

## 依赖

**必需**：DeepSeek Harness 本身（`>= 0.2.0-rc.1 < 0.3.0-0`）；运行时 **Node ≥ 22.13 或 ≥ 23.4**
（插件用内置 `node:sqlite` 读写 bili 索引，低于这个版本会打一行 `node:sqlite-unavailable` 并跳过索引部分）。

**配合**（缺了自动跳过，不会加载失败）：

| 组件 | 缺失时的表现 |
|---|---|
| `@michengai/dsh-archive-manager` | 没有「删除会话」入口，只有开机对账 |
| `billion-context` | 快照与索引两项跳过 |
| `dsh-cost-meter` | 账本与明细两项跳过 |
| `dsh-context` | 概览缓存一项跳过（默认也只报告） |

## 使用

装好后不需要任何操作。开关在 **设置 → 插件 → 插件管理 → dsh-session-leftover-purge**，改动即时生效。

| 项目 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 总开关 | 开 | 关掉后不清理，也不再监听删除 |
| bili JSON 快照 | 开 | 移走 bili 面板里该族的快照文件 |
| bili 索引 | 开 | 行、内容引用计数、三个会话键控 `kv_store` blob；写前 `VACUUM INTO` 备份 |
| cost-meter 账本明细 | 关 | 只删 `days[*].sessions[]` 里的明细行，总额不动 |
| cost-meter 明细文件 | 关 | 删掉每轮用量凭证（先复制进 trash） |
| cost-meter 改价备份报告 | 开 | 只在开机报告里列出 cost-meter 自己的 `before-reprice` 备份占用，**不删** |
| dsh-context 缓存 | 关 | 清 `overview-cache.v3` 分片里的会话条目（默认只报告） |
| archive-projcache | 关 | 清 `session_projcache` 里带会话 id 的文件（默认只报告） |
| 备份保留天数 | 7 天 | 过期即删；`0` = 永久保留 |
| 备份体积上限 | 2048 MB | 超出后从最旧批次开始删；`0` = 不限 |
| 演练模式 | 关 | 只报告，不移动也不删除（开机清扫同样遵守） |
| 开机对账 | 开 | 扫描孤儿快照族并写 `orphans.json` |
| 开机清理残留绑定 | 开 | 清 `kv_store` 里指向已删会话（含子代理）的条目，抢在 bili lane 启动前 |
| 自动清理孤儿 | 关 | 对账发现孤儿就直接清理 |
| 开机延迟 | 8000 ms | 开机对账前等待多久 |

「恢复最近备份 / 删除全部备份 / 立即备份 cost-meter 账本」三个字段是触发器：**填一个新数字并保存**
执行一次（DSH 的表单没有按钮，只能这样表达动作）。

## 会话存储后端

「这个会话还在不在」是清理前唯一要回答的问题。插件支持三种后端：

| 后端 | 判据 |
|---|---|
| `jsonl` | `$DSH_HOME/sessions/<project>/<session>/` 目录存在 |
| `sqlite` | `<sessions>/sessions.sqlite`，表名与 id 列自动探测 |
| `unknown` | 两者都读不到 |

`unknown` 一律回答"还活着"：**读不到状态时宁可不删**。开机对账在 `unknown` 下连孤儿报告都不出，
只写一行日志——避免 `自动清理孤儿` 拿到一份"全都是孤儿"的名单。

## 备份与恢复

每次清理在 `~/.dsh/storages/session-leftover-purge/trash/<时间戳>/` 留可还原副本：

- `index.db` —— 删行前的完整数据库（`VACUUM INTO` 单文件快照，旧版 SQLite 退回三文件拷贝）
- `session-…__*.json` —— 移走的 bili 快照
- `kv-store.json.bak` —— 开机清扫改写前的 `kv_store` 原始行（后缀不是 `.json`，否则会被当成快照写回 bili 目录）
- `ledger.json` —— 改账本前的完整副本
- `cost-files/`、`cache/`、`projcache/` —— 各适配器改写前的原件

恢复入口是「恢复最近备份」触发器。数据库或账本正被占用时，插件不会强写：改成
`*.restored-<时间戳>` 放在旁边，退出 DSH 后自行替换。

## 日志

`~/.dsh/storages/session-leftover-purge/`：

- `purge.log` —— 每次启动 `ready v…` + `roots state=… bili=… sessions=… store=…`，每次清理/恢复/清扫各一行
- `orphans.json` —— 最近一次对账结果（含 `store` 与 `evidence`）
- `triggers.json` —— 已执行过的触发器数字

## 边界

- 只处理 archive-manager 的右键删除；其它途径靠开机对账。
- 子代理只在父会话被清理时连带处理（DSH 不会为 `|sub:` 子会话单独发事件）。
- bili 的 lane 会把 `kv_store` 从内存写回，所以清扫必须抢在它启动之前；本机已被改过则本轮放弃
  （`changed-during-read`），下次开机再试。
- 插件自己的状态跟 `$DSH_HOME`（可用 `SESSION_LEFTOVER_PURGE_DIR` 覆盖）；bili 的数据目录是用户级的
  （`BILI_SESSIONS_DIR`），不随 profile 隔离。
- bili 的 `index.db` 属于另一个进程：`SQLITE_BUSY` 会跳过，下次再处理。
- 不碰 DSH 附件、不碰 Electron 的 localStorage。
- 任何失败都只写日志，不抛给 DSH 的删除流程。

MIT License.

DSH compatibility declares 0.2.0-rc.1 through below 0.3.0. The native removed-session hook validates session identifiers, rechecks live sessions and creates backups before plugin-data cleanup; settings also expose restore and backup deletion. SQLite/filesystem writes and purge/restore remain consequential operations. prepack builds generated files. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-smart-approval

**Smart Auto** —— 一个更懂上下文的审批评审档，给 DeepSeek Harness 用。

它把"每一次工具调用都问一遍模型"换成"**只有越出工作区沙箱的那一下才评审**"，
并且会把**人工裁决**沉淀成可复用的先例，让"相似但不同"的后续调用自动放行。

---

## 1. 它解决什么

| 常见问题 | 本插件的做法 |
|---|---|
| 官方 Auto review 每次工具调用都调模型 | 只在**沙箱升级**时评审（预设沙箱 = `workspace-write`） |
| 官方插件给 Codex 路由发 `temperature`，被上游拒绝 | 请求里**不出现** `temperature` |
| 分类器看不到历史决定，"相似但不同"无法复用 | 读取**工作区先例**注入评审提示词 |
| 判定失败会静默放行或直接拒绝 | 一律 `next()` 交给人工，**fail-open-to-human** |
| 重复调用反复评审、成本不可见 | 相同 `tool+args` 缓存 8h；带 `/smart-report` 台账 |

## 2. 权限档

安装后权限选择器多出 **Smart Auto**（`smart-auto`）：

- 沙箱：`workspace-write`
- 审批策略：`ask`
- 只有该档下本插件应答；其它档（`workspace-write` / `sandboxed-auto` / `auto` /
  `danger-full-access`）原样交给下游

## 3. 一次调用的完整决策链

```
工具调用
  └─ 是否需要沙箱升级？
       ├─ 否（工作区内）           → 直接执行，不评审、不打扰
       └─ 是 → approval/request
              ├─ 本插件（仅在 smart-auto 档）
              │    ├─ 命中判定缓存           → allowed-once（毫秒级）
              │    ├─ 模型判定 allow         → allowed-once（并写台账）
              │    └─ 模型判定 ask / 超时 /
              │       解析失败 / 异常        → next()（交人工）
              └─ 其它档 → 下游应答者（人工 / 其它插件）
```

人工裁决后（`allowed-once` / `rejected`）：

```
session/event: approval/asked → approval/decided
   ├─ 是插件自己批的（selfAllowed）→ 跳过（防自我强化）
   └─ 是人工裁决 → 小模型蒸馏成一行动作类别
                  → ~/.dsh/smart-approval/precedents/<sha256(cwd)[:12]>.jsonl
                  → 下次评审注入提示词
```

## 4. 配置

```yaml
- id: smart-approval
  config:
    presetName: smart-auto              # 应答的权限档
    provider: deepseek-account          # 评审模型 provider（留空跟随默认）
    model: deepseek-flash               # 评审模型
    timeoutMs: 20000                    # 单次评审/蒸馏超时（超时→人工）
    maxInputTokens: 6000                # 评审输入预算（证据+上下文+先例）
    cacheTtlMs: 28800000                # 判定缓存（8h）
    precedentsEnabled: true
    precedentsDir: ~/.dsh/smart-approval/precedents
    distillOnHumanDecision: true        # 人工裁决后自动蒸馏先例
    maxPrecedentLines: 200              # 单工作区先例上限（超出裁剪）
    ledger: true
    ledgerPath: ~/.dsh/smart-approval/ledger.jsonl
    maxLedgerLines: 500
    reportCommand: smart-report         # 斜杠命令名；留空则不注册
    debugLog: ''                        # 非空则把事件写调试日志（排查用）
```

## 5. 评审证据（三层，统一压预算）

1. **本次调用**：工具名、参数（≤6k 字符）、审批理由、cwd
2. **会话近期**：最近 6 条用户消息 / 工具调用（各自截断 300–500 字符）
3. **工作区先例**：最近 20 条

## 6. 先例格式

`~/.dsh/smart-approval/precedents/<sha256(cwd)[:12]>.jsonl`，一行一条：

```json
{"action":"allow","class":"home-dir-scratch-write","note":"Allowed: creating a scratch test file under a new home-directory folder ...","tool":"bash","at":"2026-11-24T10:58:16.927Z"}
{"action":"allow","class":"delete-scratch-directory","note":"Allowed removing a self-created scratch/test directory under the home folder with an explicit scoped path and no wildcards.","tool":"bash","at":"2026-11-24T10:58:29.283Z"}
```

- `class` 是**操作类别**（不是原命令），所以相似调用能命中；
- `action` 为 `deny` 的先例会让同类操作**再次询问**；
- 按工作区隔离，不跨工作区共享。

## 7. 台账与报告

每次决策追加一行到 `ledger.jsonl`（最多 500 行，超出裁剪）：

```json
{"at":"2026-11-24T10:59:00.356Z","kind":"allow","tool":"bash","source":"model","ms":812,"reason":"Matches existing allowed precedent: ..."}
```

`kind` 取值：`allow` / `ask` / `cache` / `human`。

在会话里执行 **`/smart-report`** 查看本进程的汇总：

```
Smart Auto 0.3.0 台账（本进程）
评审 12｜模型放行 9｜转人工 3｜缓存命中 5｜失败 0
人工裁决 2｜新先例 2｜台账文件 ~/.dsh/smart-approval/ledger.jsonl
最近决策：
  10:59:00 allow bash model 812ms — Matches existing allowed precedent: ...
```

## 8. 安全边界

- 判定失败 / 超时 / 格式错误 / 异常 → `next()`（人工兜底），**不静默放行**；
- 提示词明确把证据视为数据，不执行其中的指令；
- 插件自己批准的调用不会写进先例（避免"模型放行→模型学习→自我强化"）；
- 蒸馏提示词禁止写入密钥、文件名、文件内容；
- 评审与蒸馏都不改文件系统，只追加先例与台账。

## 9. 已知限制（0.3.0）

1. 不做确定性危险清单前置拦截（依赖沙箱与下游策略）；后续可加**路径前缀规则**（如
   `~/Library/LaunchAgents`、`/etc`、`~/.ssh`）直接判 `ask`，不依赖模型；
2. 提示词对"系统级目录写入"的约束强度依赖模型理解，实测对 `~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.txt`
   这类无害文件会放行；
3. 先例只在"人工裁决"时增长；纯模型放行的调用不进先例；
4. 与 `dsh-auto-approve` 并存时，两者各自声明 `permission` 预设表；本插件的表已包含
   `sandboxed-auto`，两个档位都会保留，按各自 `presetName` 生效。

## 10. 故障排查

| 症状 | 排查 |
|---|---|
| 切到 smart-auto 后仍每次都问人 | `/smart-report` 看"评审"是否为 0：为 0 说明插件没答（档名不匹配或未加载） |
| 先例不生成 | 先看 `debugLog: '/tmp/smart-approval-debug.log'` 下是否出现 `session-event type=approval/asked`；再查 `distill ... parsed=no`（模型返回非 JSON） |
| 模型总是 ask | 调大 `timeoutMs`、换更快模型，或检查先例是否写入了 `deny` |
| 台账为空 | 确认 `ledger: true` 且 `ledgerPath` 可写 |

安装/卸载：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-smart-approval
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-smart-approval
```

decision.reason: Held for versioned DSH compatibility, runtime execution policy acceptance. MIT and local-checkout installation are documented. The native hook can return allow for a sandbox escalation using an LLM decision and persisted human-decision precedents; its patch modifies permission presets. A versioned DSH contract and acceptance of that approval policy are unresolved. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# @gavinc-cn/dsh-plugins-runtime 把**宿主（node）侧运行**的自研插件收成一个可安装单位的 bundle 包：装上它，Plugins 面板里多出 一张标题为**包名**的卡片（`@gavinc-cn/dsh-plugins-runtime`）；卡片里的每个**组件**（组合行）= 一个**独立开关**。 > 标题为什么是包名：面板标题的取值链是「`locale/*.json` 的 `meta.title` → 缺省回落 `package.json` > 的 `name`」。本包**故意不写 `meta.title`**（2026-10-15 起），只保留 `meta.description` 供描述 > 本地化 —— 这样卡片标题与 `@gavinc-cn/touchstone-dsh` 一样直接显示包名。 - **一个包 = 面板一张卡片**：包名出现在 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里，本包的 `cordis.patch.yml` 就会被当作一个配置层叠加进组合树。 - **组件 = 行 = 开关**：本包每条 `- insert:` 声明一个组件；行状态（`disabled`）由各 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 覆盖行持有，面板里拨开关就是往那里写回。 - **整包开关**：包名在不在 `dsh.profile.bundles`（改它要重启宿主）。 ## 归属判据 包内组件都是**宿主（node）侧的运行支撑**：记忆、提交/文件/git 守卫、路径规则闸门、 沙箱升权等 —— 它们的 package.json 里**没有** `dsh.client` 声明。 面向 Web GUI 的组件（含纯浏览器组件，以及 2026-10-15 从本包移出的 `dsh-patch-ask-expand`）在 [@gavinc-cn/dsh-plugins-ui](../dsh-plugins-ui/README.md)。归属判据自 2026-10-15 起是 **「面向谁」而不是「代码跑在哪」**：`dsh-patch-ask-expand` 的运行体确实在宿主侧（启动时对官方 `dsh-client-ui-tool` 的 client bundle 打文本补丁），但它是纯 GUI 观感功能 ⇒ 归 UI 包， 免得「只想装 UI 包」的人发现不了它。两个包合起来 = **18 行**（UI 10 + 本包 8）。 `kanban-board`、`sandbox-path-allowlist` 与 `dsh-readonly-guard` 不随任何 bundle 下发 （`sandbox-path-allowlist` 2026-10-17 由 `dsh-path-rules` 合并退役、`dsh-readonly-guard` 2026-10-24 退役，白名单/只读判定能力分别由 `dsh-path-rules` 与第五/六档 + 原生沙箱承接）； `dsh-autocommit` 2026-11-01 迁入 `@gavinc-cn/touchstone-dsh` 的 bundle patch（行 id 全树唯一， 两边都带会判 unaddressable），本仓只留包体作真源。 ## 安装 ```bash # 装进某个 profile（pnpm 会把 optionalDependencies 里的 8 个组件包一并装上； # 镜像缺个别包时只跳过那一个，见下一节） dsh plugin --profile web add @gavinc-cn/dsh-plugins-runtime ``` - CLI 这条路径会在 pnpm 成功后**自动**把新 bundle 追加进 `dsh.profile.bundles`（装完即启用）。 - 走 **Plugins 面板**的安装入口则**不会**自动选择 bundle，装完要自己把整包开关打开。 - **`dsh.profile.bundles` 与 `dependencies` 两处都要有本包名**：前者决定是否作为配置层加载， 后者决定面板里卡片是否显示（客户端按 `installed` 过滤，只看 `dependencies`）。 - 改了 `dsh.profile.bundles` 要**重启宿主**才生效（启动时读）；profile patch 层是 live 热重载， 行级开关不需要重启。 ### 组件依赖是可选的（2026-11-19 起，缺包不阻塞整包） 8 个组件包写在 `optionalDependencies` 里：镜像缺某个组件时，pnpm 只跳过那一个，其余组件和 bundle 本体照常安装（pnpm 12.4.1 实测）。bundle 仍会进入 `dsh.profile.bundles`；缺失组件的行仍留在 组合树里，宿主启动时只打一条 warning（非 required 行不阻断启动），面板里该行显示为 failed， 其他行不受影响。**装成功 ≠ 8 个组件都在**：缺失的包补装后重启宿主（重跑 `dsh plugin --profile

install`，或镜像恢复后重装本包）即可恢复。若手里已有缺失包的 tgz， 可以在 profile 的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 用 `file:` overrides 补上，保留完整 8 个组件。 ## 组件（8 个） | 行 id | 包 | 做什么 | |---|---|---| | `dsh-superpowers-priming` | `@gavinc-cn/dsh-superpowers-priming` | 给「重开的会话」补一份 superpowers 开场说明（按会话历史判重，不重复注入） | | `dsh-memory` | `@gavinc-cn/dsh-memory` | 跨会话记忆：首轮注入两级记忆索引，回合收尾限流提示写记忆 | | `dsh-git-guard` | `@gavinc-cn/dsh-git-guard` | git 操作归属守卫（按提交前缀/分支命名判定，拦下越权 git 写操作） | | `dsh-file-guard` | `@gavinc-cn/dsh-file-guard` | 回合收尾比对「本会话写下的文件」与磁盘漂移，只报告不自动改回 | | `dsh-path-rules` | `@gavinc-cn/dsh-path-rules` | 第五权限模式「路径规则」的逐调用闸门：项目内可读写 / 项目外读允许·写审批 / 白名单直通 / 黑名单读写都审批 / bash·pwsh 只读放行。**只在预设身份为 `path-rules` 时介入**，其余四档完全空转（2026-10-17 起承接退役的 `sandbox-path-allowlist` 白名单能力；`autoWhitelist` 可把用户批准的升权写入目录自动记入白名单）。**v2（0.1.2）**：判不出读写的命令交给沙箱在运行时拦写（`unanalyzable: pass`）、判不出的命令做黑名单文本粗检（`opaqueBlacklistScan`）。**v3（0.2.0，2026-10-24）**：`staticGate: true`（默认）保留逐调用静态判定；配置 `staticGate: false` 后写判定交给执行层多根件（`dsh-sandbox-whitelist` + `dsh-fs-whitelist`），本插件只留黑名单与审批学习；预置升权 `preemptiveWhitelistEscalation` 已删除 | | `dsh-write-guard` | `@gavinc-cn/dsh-write-guard` | 第六权限模式「完全权限（拦截）」的逐调用写入闸门：读任意文件 / 项目内 / 白名单写直通，越界写弹框并自动学习白名单，判不出的 `bash`·`pwsh` 交当前会话模型判定。**只在预设身份为 `write-guard` 时介入**，其余档位完全空转；插件停用 = 完全不拦截 | | `dsh-sandbox-whitelist` | `@gavinc-cn/dsh-sandbox-whitelist` | 多根沙箱 provider（方案 C，Linux + Windows）：顶替官方 `- id: sandbox`，把项目根 + 白名单根 + 临时区变成执行层可写根（Linux bwrap/Landlock；Windows 官方 windows-acl 受限令牌 + 写 SID ACE），其余只读；只对
